Stopping the tool-call attempts here: I did not run any code, so I have no computed values for K_{m,n} and no verified formula.

What I did establish by hand is the P3 case, K_{1,2} (m=2, n=1), under the reading that pebbles may be discarded. Its largest unsolvable configuration has 6 pebbles, for example (5,0,1) or (3,0,3) on the three vertices in path order. So stack(K_{1,2}) = 7 under the threshold reading. That is one data point, and I have not verified it against an exhaustive search.

I cannot give a verified closed form for stack(K_{m,n}) from this. A formula consistent with the single data point (for example 2^{m+1}-1, which gives 7 at m=2) is only a guess. I have no evidence that it holds for general m ≥ n ≥ 1.

To finish, the search script should enumerate all configurations of size up to some bound on K_{m,n} for small m,n, mark each as solvable or not by DFS over pebbling moves (discarding allowed), and take the largest unsolvable size plus one. That would give values for several (m,n) to fit a formula.

ANSWER: Not determined (unverified guess: 2^{m+1}-1)
